title: Running is not recovered
question: Can the payment service resume traffic when compute and a readable backup are available but identity, keys, network paths, or acceptance remain unresolved?
scenario: Ransomware has disabled the primary payment environment. Recovery compute is running and an older immutable backup is readable in a separate account. Identity-provider readiness and the key-management route are still unknown, DNS has not been switched, and business owners have not reconciled transactions since the recovery point.
focalRelation: A protected copy supports trusted data only after validation; application start depends on identity, keys, and network; resuming traffic additionally requires technical, security, and business acceptance.

states.title: Expose the dependency graph
states.caption: Compute and a backup are visible alongside identity, keys, network, transaction state, and the three acceptance gates.

states.title: Validate the recovery copy
states.caption: Restore and integrity checks produce a candidate data state; the RPO gap remains explicit.

states.title: Find the first blockers
states.caption: The application still cannot start because identity, KMS, and network readiness are unresolved.

states.title: Start under controlled conditions
states.caption: After identity, key, and network checks pass, the application starts at reduced capacity; start is not yet recovery acceptance.

states.title: Evaluate three acceptance gates
states.caption: Operations verifies capacity and monitoring; security validates access and hardening; business owners reconcile transactions and the data gap.

statuses.accept: technical pass; security pass; business pending

states.title: Resume with limits recorded
states.caption: Traffic resumes only after all gates pass, with the reduced-capacity QoS plan, residual RPO gap, owners, and failback criteria documented.

variants.label: Two sites, one dependency

states.caption: Neither site becomes usable while the shared identity service is unavailable; simultaneous operation also exceeds the shared team.

states.title: Require tested alternatives

prediction.prompt: Compute is running and the immutable backup is readable, but identity and KMS readiness are unknown. May customer traffic resume?

options.label: No; validate dependencies and all acceptance gates first
options.feedback: Correct. Identify the first blockers, then distinguish application start from accepted service recovery.

options.label: Yes; compute and a readable backup prove recovery.
options.feedback: Component availability does not prove decryptability, authorization, transaction integrity, capacity, or business acceptance.

options.label: Yes; immutability makes further validation unnecessary.
options.feedback: Immutability helps protect a copy. It does not prove currency, key access, dependencies, or usable service.

prediction.hint: Separate copy readability, application start, and permission to resume business traffic.

transfer.prompt: Two sites have independent compute and storage, but both use one unavailable identity provider and one operations team. What does the second site prove?

options.label: It proves resilience because the sites are geographically separate.
options.feedback: Geographic diversity does not remove shared identity or staffing failure modes.

options.label: It improves infrastructure options but leaves common dependencies unresolved
options.feedback: Correct. Tested alternatives for identity and staffing are needed before claiming service resilience.

options.label: A DNS switch alone makes either site usable.
options.feedback: Routing traffic cannot repair unavailable identity or insufficient operational capacity.

transfer.hint: Trace dependencies that both sites still share.

retry.prompt: A database cluster fails over, but the secondary has half the capacity and its key route is unmonitored. What is the sound operating decision?

options.label: Declare full recovery because failover completed.
options.feedback: Failover is a transition, not proof of adequate capacity, keys, monitoring, or business acceptance.

options.label: Immediately fail back without validation to restore full capacity.
options.feedback: Failback is another risky change and needs its own readiness and validation checks.

options.label: Throttle service, verify key and monitoring paths, then seek acceptance
options.feedback: Correct. Operate within known capacity while validating dependencies and acceptance criteria.

retry.hint: Treat failover, capacity, dependency health, and acceptance as separate decisions.

takeaway: Recovery is a dependency and acceptance claim: verified copies enable restoration, dependencies enable start, and technical, security, and business gates enable controlled service use.
assumptions: The 23-minute gap and 50% capacity are scenario values, not universal thresholds.
The dependency arrows express prerequisites, not elapsed recovery time.
Business acceptance includes transaction reconciliation for this payment scenario.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The state model preserves the combined data, identity, key-management, DNS/network, people/vendor, validation, and resume-traffic dependencies and recomputes a shared-identity-provider failure. Learners inspect authored dependency states rather than independently manipulating every dependency and backup age, so it is equivalent.
